sections.bodyText: A black hole is a region of space where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape once it crosses a boundary called the event horizon. Black holes form when massive stars, at least a few times heavier than our sun, run out of nuclear fuel and collapse under their own gravity at the end of their lives. The point at the very center of a black hole, where all of its mass is compressed into an infinitely small point, is called a singularity, and our current understanding of physics breaks down there. Black holes come in different sizes: stellar black holes form from collapsing stars, while supermassive black holes, millions or even billions of times the mass of the sun, sit at the centers of most large galaxies, including our own Milky Way. Because black holes don't emit light themselves, scientists detect them indirectly, by observing how their gravity affects nearby stars and gas, or by capturing the glow of superheated material spiraling into them. In 2019, astronomers released the first-ever direct image of a black hole's silhouette, located in the galaxy M87, confirming decades of theoretical predictions.

summary:
- A black hole is a region of space with gravity so strong that not even light can escape.
- The event horizon is the boundary beyond which nothing can return from a black hole.
- Black holes form when massive stars collapse after running out of nuclear fuel.
- To form a black hole, a star needs to be at least a few times heavier than the sun.
- The singularity is the point at the center of a black hole where mass is infinitely compressed.
- Current physics cannot adequately describe conditions at the singularity.
- Stellar black holes result from the collapse of stars.
- Supermassive black holes, millions or billions of times the sun's mass, are found at galaxy centers.
- The Milky Way contains a supermassive black hole at its center.
- Black holes are detected indirectly by observing gravitational effects on nearby stars and gas.
- The glow of superheated material spiraling into black holes helps in their indirect detection.
- In 2019, the first direct image of a black hole's silhouette was captured.
- The imaged black hole is located in the galaxy M87.
- The 2019 image confirmed decades of theoretical predictions about black holes.
